items.title: Reliance Entertainment admitted to insolvency over ₹11.94 crore debt linked to movie Auron Mein Kahan Dum Tha
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at Mumbai has admitted Reliance Entertainment Studios Private Limited to the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) over a ₹11.94 crore default linked to the release of the film Auron Mein Kahan Dum Tha . By way of an order passed on August 19, a bench of judicial member Nilesh Sharma and technical member Sameer Kakar held that the ₹20 crore advanced by Pen India to finance the release of the film Auron Mein Kahan Dum Tha constituted financial debt under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The NCLT imposed a moratorium under Section 14 of the IBC and appointed Umesh Balaram Sonkar as the interim resolution professional. It, however, clarified that it has not crystallised the amount claimed by Pen India and left its collation to the interim resolution professional. The amount was advanced to Reliance under a security deposit agreement executed in November 2022. The agreement required the company to repay it with interest at 21 percent per annum, compounded monthly. Friday Filmworks Private Limited, partly owned by Reliance, subsequently paid ₹15 crore to Pen India under an additional agreement executed in October 2023. ₹4.49 crore, along with ₹7.44 crore in interest, remained outstanding as principal, as per Pen India. Reliance Entertainment Studios argued that the transaction was expressly described as a security deposit and not a money-lending arrangement. It also contended that its liability stood extinguished under a clause requiring repayment through a third-party satellite or digital rights provider. The NCLT rejected these arguments, holding that the substance and commercial effect of a transaction, rather than the label attached to it, determines whether it is financial debt. “ The transaction, therefore, possesses all the essential attributes of a borrowing notwithstanding the terminology adopted by the parties ,” the tribunal said. It added that the contractual clause relied upon by Reliance merely created an additional payment mechanism and did not extinguish the company’s primary liability. The Bench noted that Reliance had repeatedly acknowledged the outstanding amount after the ₹15 crore payment. In April 2024, it proposed paying the balance in two instalments by June 30 and September 30, 2024. items.title: Delhi HC rejects Khan Market Association's plea seeking uniform valuation method to determine property tax
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday rejected a plea by Khan Market Welfare Association seeking directions to the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) to adopt a uniform valuation method for calculating property tax in its jurisdiction [Khan Market Welfare Association v UOI & Ors] . NDMC area includes locations such as Connaught Place, Khan Market, Chanakyapuri and many other posh commercial and residential locations in Lutyens' Delhi. A Division Bench of Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Shail Jain dismissed the plea, holding that the Court cannot issue directions on how a statutory authority like NDMC should formulate and administer the methodology for determination of rateable value (an official estimate of a property's annual open-market rental value). “The Court cannot, under the guise of issuing a mandamus, substitute its own formulation for that of the competent statutory authority. The principle is not that the exercise of statutory power is immune from judicial review, rather, it is that judicial review is directed towards the legality of the exercise of power and not towards the Court itself undertaking the function entrusted to the statutory authority,” the Court observed. The Bench also rejected the association’s plea to constitute an expert committee to inquire into alleged frauds, irregularities and discrepancies in the fixation of rateable values throughout the jurisdiction of the NDMC. “A direction of this nature would require the Court to create an administrative mechanism, prescribe its composition and remit, and entrust it with functions which have not been shown to have been statutorily vested in such a body. The jurisdiction under Article 226 cannot ordinarily be invoked for creation of such an institutional mechanism merely because the Petitioner alleges irregularities in the functioning of a statutory authority,” it ruled. Justice Anil Kshetarpal and Justice Shail Jain The Khan Market Welfare Association approached the High Court seeking directions to the NDMC to adopt a uniform valuation method until the Unit Area Method (UAM) was formally implemented. It also sought constitution of an expert committee to probe alleged irregularities, and strict compliance with various provisions of the NDMC Act. It was argued that NDMC was drawing on the UAM, actual rent, comparable rent and historical values to determine rateable values for similarly placed properties in areas like Khan Market and Connaught Place, resulting in wide disparities in tax liability

items.title: When old statutes meet new codes: The conundrum with India’s Labour Codes and State-specific legislations
items.summary: The field of labour and employment in India has traditionally been vast and fragmented, governed by various legislations at the Central and State level. As a result, there has always existed a wide array of legislations which were required to be examined independently and cohesively, to identify the compliance requirements and the provisions that were applicable to employees. During the years 2019 and 2020, a progressive and revolutionary step was taken towards attempting to simplify the labour laws in the country by consolidating labour legislations into the four Labour Codes. While the Central government has brought the Labour Codes along with the Central Rules into force and effect, a majority of the states are still in the process of finalising and issuing the final State Rules to each Code. Among the four Codes, the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, has become paramount in governing the working conditions of workers/ employees, specifically regulating the day-to-day aspects of employment, such as working hours, leave, etc., and this is being provided for under one specific statute. Therefore, on paper, the introduction of the OSH Code was meant to be a moment of simplification, promising employers a single and predictable compliance framework and allowing employees to easily understad their working conditions and entitlements. In practice, however, the simplification has been incomplete. Most States in India have an independent legislation that governs shops and commercial establishments and in addition to registration requirements, also provide for working hours, leave, process of termination and such other aspects which governs the working conditions of employees. The position that remains now is trying to understand the OSH Code along with the applicable state specific shops and commercial establishments law, taking employers and employees back to the pre-labour code era where multiple legislations were required to be read together to be able to best comply with the applicable law. One may argue that the Labour Codes have an overreaching effect and will apply notwithstanding any other applicable law, as the repeal provision in the OSH Code relates to the Code stating that it will be the law that is applicable even when there is another law that is inconsistent with the Code. items.summary: A munsiff court in Kerala's Ernakulam has passed an interim injunction restraining social media platforms and the makers of Malayalam web series 'Anali' from releasing, promoting, streaming or circulating the show on any over the top platform [ Jollyamma Joseph @ Jolly v JioHotstar Pvt Ltd& ors ]. Judge Reeja R Nair passed the order on August 20 on a plea filed by Jolly, the prime accused in the Koodathayi killings. The Court restrained the web series makers from releasing, publishing, promoting, exhibiting, hosting, reproducing or streaming the web series or any related promotional material to the extent it identifies Jolly with the principal female character and creates an impression that she is the actual perpetrator of the offences in question. The order was passed months after the Kerala High Court had declined to entertain a similar plea filed by Jolly seeking to restrain the show's broadcast. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas had then held that Jolly had an alternative remedy available to her which she was yet to exhaust an appeal under Rule 12 of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, after her representation to the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (later forwarded to JioHotstar) came to be rejected. She is currently lodged at the women's prison in Kozhikode, with criminal trials against her pending at different stages across multiple cases. items.title: Should right to work be made fundamental right? Supreme Court on plea for minimum wage in rural employment schemes
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday questioned whether the statutory guarantee of employment for rural workers can be placed on the same footing as the fundamental right to life and dignity under Article 21 [Aruna Roy v. Union of India] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted that the Constitution does not recognise the right to work as a fundamental right. Instead, the Court observed, the Constitution places it among the State's obligations under the Directive Principles of State Policy. “The Constitution does not make the right to work a fundamental right. In fact, it is only a democratic aspiration under Part IV. To achieve that aspiration, the State formulates a policy where work is provided at a graded compensatory level. Should we create it on a par with Article 21?” said Justice Bagchi. He then flagged the broader constitutional implications of elevating the right to work to the level of an enforceable right, particularly if the State were to scale back its social welfare measures. “That is a very big question which we need to answer. Because if we do that, and the State contracts its social welfare activities, can we issue a mandamus upon them and say, no, you have to implement Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) or the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (BG RAM) scheme?” asked Justice Bagchi. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court made the observations while hearing a petition concerning payment of minimum wages and compensation for delayed wages to workers under the rural employment guarantee scheme. Advocate Prashant Bhushan argued that the petition was not rendered infructuous by the replacement of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act. The plea before the Court concerns two issues: compensation for delayed payment of MGNREGA wages and whether workers can be paid less than minimum wages notified by the respective States. The Supreme Court had earlier dealt with delayed payment of MGNREGA wages in the Swaraj Abhiyan v Union of India judgment. Today, CJI Kant said that the issue stood covered by that judgment and that any failure to implement that judgment would constitute a fresh cause of action. items.title: Supreme Court urges Matrimony.com, Jodi365 to tie the knot and settle
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed its disinclination to entertain a plea filed by Matrimony.com challenging a Madras High Court judgment restraining it from using ‘Jodii’ for its matchmaking application [ Matrimony.com Limited v FreeElective Network Private Limited ]. However, instead of dismissing the plea today, a Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe gave Matrimony.com and Jodi365 an opportunity to explore an amicable resolution. Matrimony.com offered to rename its application “Jodi Matrimony” to avoid abruptly shutting down the business and affecting its existing users. The Bench asked the parties to discuss this proposal and indicated that it would consider the matter again if they were unable to arrive at a settlement. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The dispute arose after Matrimony.com launched its ‘Jodii’ mobile application in October 2021. FreeElective Network Private Limited, which operates the matchmaking platform Jodi365, issued a cease-and-desist notice against this move. It subsequently filed a trademark infringement and passing-off suit before the Madras High Court against Matrimony.com. FreeElective claimed that it had been using ‘Jodi365’ since 2009 and had registered it as a composite device mark in 2010. It alleged that Matrimony.com’s adoption of the phonetically similar ‘Jodii’ for identical services was likely to confuse consumers. Matrimony.com countered that FreeElective's trademark registration protected only the composite ‘Jodi365’ mark and did not give FreeElective exclusive rights over the word ‘Jodi’. It argued that ‘Jodi’, meaning a couple or pair, was descriptive of matchmaking services and was widely used by other matrimonial and dating platforms. In July 2022, a single judge of the Madras High Court dismissed FreeElective’s suit. The judge found that while the composite ‘Jodi365’ mark had acquired distinctiveness, the constituent word ‘Jodi’ remained descriptive and non-distinctive. A High Court Division Bench of Justices P Velmurugan and K Govindarajan Thilakavadi, however, overturned the single-judge ruling on August 11, 2026. The High Court consequently restrained Matrimony.com from infringing the ‘Jodi365’ trademark or passing off its services by using ‘Jodii’ or any other deceptively similar mark. items.title: Arbitrators move Supreme Court after Rajasthan HC cuts their fees citing delay; SC also says "delay is too much"
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently expressed serious concern over the time and costs involved in arbitration proceedings, observing that prolonged hearings defeat the very purpose of choosing arbitration as an alternative to conventional litigation. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observations while hearing appeals filed by arbitral tribunal members in a case arising from the arbitration between HCL Infosystems Limited and Rajasthan power distribution companies including Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited. The arbitral proceedings had commenced in 2020 and 198 hearings had been held with substantial amounts having been paid towards arbitral fees. The process was yet to conclude. The Rajasthan High Court had taken exception to the delay in arbitration and had ordered a 5 percent reduction in the fees charged by arbitrators from April 2025. This prompted the arbitrators to approach the Supreme Court. However, the top court also said the delay was "too long". Justice Bagchi asked whether an arbitration that continued for years could serve its intended purpose. "We talk about an arbitration-friendly environment and look at this. This is egregious. items.summary: OP Jindal Global University (JGU) has set up a Chief Justices of India Museum on its campus in Sonipat, dedicated to the lives and legacies of those who have helmed the Supreme Court of India. Vice Chancellor (VC) Prof (Dr) C Raj Kumar said, "It is first of its kind, not only in India but, to the best of our knowledge, anywhere in the world." He added that the museum builds on JGU's Constitution Museum and that together, the two initiatives create a space to understand the constitutional and judicial journey of the country. Chief Justices of India Museum, OP Jindal Global University An introductory note issued by the University said that the museum extends the Constitution's vision of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity by focusing on the Supreme Court's role in giving those ideals life through its jurisprudence, institutional leadership and commitment to constitutional governance. Chief Justices of India Museum, OP Jindal Global University Through judicial archives, landmark judgments, personal memorabilia, photographs, multimedia installations and stories of judicial courage, the museum aims to make this journey accessible to scholars, students and citizens alike. The note added that the museum is not merely a repository of judicial history but a space for understanding the ideas, institutions and individuals that have shaped the Republic's constitutional life. Chief Justices of India Museum, OP Jindal Global University Each Chief Justice, the note said, represents a distinct chapter in the evolution of India's constitutional democracy. The museum, it added, invites visitors not only to look back at the Supreme Court's history but also to reflect on the values that should guide its future. "Universities have a special responsibility to preserve knowledge while nurturing constitutional understanding, critical inquiry and informed citizenship. In this spirit, the Museum of the Chief Justices of India seeks to become a lasting institution of learning, reflection and public engagement. items.title: Muthanga land agitation case: Kerala High Court suspends sentences of M Geethanandan, 3 others
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday suspended the sentences imposed on activist M Geethanandan and three others convicted in an attempt to murder case arising from the 2003 Muthanga land struggle. Justice A Badharudeen passed the order on appeals filed by social activist M Geethanandan, Binu, Ramesan and Anilkumar, who were found guilty by a sessions court and sentenced to five years in jail over a violent confrontation between police and adivasi protesters at the Muthanga in 2003 The High Court had earlier observed that the trial court's finding on criminal conspiracy under Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) was only prima facie in nature, and not conclusive. Justice A Badharudeen The Muthanga land struggle stemmed from an eviction drive carried out by the Kerala Police at the Muthanga Wildlife Sanctuary in Wayanad in 2003. The eviction drive led to a violent confrontation between the police and Adivasi protesters, which escalated into police firing. Five protesters and police constable KV Vinod died in the incident. A sessions court found them guilty of offences including attempt to murder Senior Civil Police Officer Abdul Salam, kidnapping Forest Range Officer PK Sasidharan, causing grievous hurt with dangerous weapons, wrongful restraint, unlawful assembly and offences against public order. They were sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for five years and payment of fines. However, they were acquitted of the charge relating to the death of constable Vinod. The appellants moved the High Court contending that their conviction could not be sustained on the basis of the sessions court finding relating to criminal conspiracy. The Court has now suspended their sentences and granted them bail subject to conditions. items.title: Supreme Court reduces law practice criterion to become civil judge from 3 years to 1 year but adds clerkship and training criteria
items.summary: In a key judgment on recruitment of judicial officers, the Supreme Court on Friday upheld its May 2025 ruling that mandated law practice as a condition for entry into judicial service, but reduced the experience prescribed at the bar from 3 years to 1 year. Pertinently, the candidates who succeed at the judicial service exam will have to undergo one year of intensive training at the State Judicial Academy followed by six months’ clerkship under the District Judge/Higher Judicial Service and six months under a sitting High Court judge. This will effectively be a substitute for the remaining 2 years practice which was prescribed by the earlier judgment. However, these rules will become applicable only from April 1, 2027. The Court has granted a key exemption with regard to a transition period running up to March 31, 2027. For candidates applying within that date, no law practice experience would be required and they shall be deemed to have completed one-year law practice. "The direction is that all law graduates will be eligible to apply notwithstanding the three-year practice requirement, having regard to the fact that more than one year has elapsed since the judgment under review was pronounced. Such candidates, for the purposes of their applications, will be deemed to have completed one year of active practice and shall not be required to produce a certificate of practice in respect of the said period," the Court said. However, they have to undergo the training and clerkship as prescribed. "Candidates seeking to pursue the aforesaid recruitment shall, upon appointment, be designated as Trainee Judicial Officers. They shall undergo one year of intensive training at the concerned State Judicial Academy. This will, in effect, be equivalent to one year of practice at the Bar for the purposes of the three-year requirement," the order said During the period of such training, the Trainee Judicial Officer shall receive an emolument equivalent to one-half of the gross remuneration payable to a Judicial Magistrate First Class. items.title: Strange that 23 cops feared his katta: Allahabad HC orders CBI probe into police encounter of accused
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the alleged encounter shooting of a man accused of attempting to open fire on a police team deployed to arrest him in an abduction case [ Chotkau Alias Allauddin v State of UP and 4 Others ]. Justice Subhash Vidyarthi directed the CBI to conduct an independent inquiry into the correctness of the allegations in the FIR lodged against Chhotkau alias Allauddin, who was shot in both legs by the police in May 2025. The Court also directed that the shooting capacity of the then Station House Officer (SHO) of Ikauna police station, Ashwini Kumar Dubey, be assessed to determine whether he could have aimed and fired a 9 mm service pistol from a distance of 15 metres at night, allegedly merely by hearing the sound of a weapon being loaded by the accused. The Court called it strange that a police team of 13 persons and a SWAT team of 10 persons had been frightened and called for further reinforcement to tackle a person carrying a katta (country-made pistol) with merely two cartridges. "It is also strange that (23) police persons armed with weapons were attacked by the revisionist carrying a katta (country-made pistol) and he had merely two cartridges with him, one of which was used by him and the other was recovered by the police ... The Court has serious apprehensions regarding the correctness of the narration made in the FIR and the manner of investigation conducted by the police. Prima facie, it appears that the narration is false,” the Bench said on August 13. items.title: College won’t lose Malayalam minority status merely because Nairs dominate management: Madras HC
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently refused to cancel the Malayalam linguistic minority status of Sree Ayyappa College for Women in Nagercoil over allegations that members of the Nair community dominated its management [Srinivasa Menon Vs State of Tamil Nadu]. A Bench of Justices CV Karthikeyan and R Sakthivel held that even if the institution’s present office-bearers were predominantly Nairs, that by itself would not affect its minority status so long as they were Malayalees and did not act against the interests of the Malayalam-speaking linguistic minority in Tamil Nadu. The judgment was delivered on August 18 while dismissing a public interest litigation filed by S Srinivasan Menon, founder trustee of Devi Seva Sangam. Menon had sought cancellation of the linguistic minority status of the college and the Sree Ayyappa College Educational Society, which runs it. The college was granted Malayalam linguistic minority status in 1987 and receives financial aid from the Tamil Nadu government. Justices Karthikeyan and Sakthivel of Madras HC The petitioner’s principal allegation was that although the college was formally a Malayalam linguistic minority institution, it was in reality being controlled by the Kerala-based Nair Service Society. He alleged that important posts in the college and its managing society were occupied by members of the Nair community from Kerala. He also claimed that 45 out of 49 teachers were Nairs and alleged irregularities in appointments, admissions and finances. Menon further relied on the fact that the college displayed photographs of Mannathu Padmanabhan, founder of the Nair Service Society, in its calendars, magazines and prospectus and declared holidays on his birth and death anniversaries. The Court, however, said that the college’s minority status was based on language and not caste. “ Even if the present office bearers are predominantly from Nair community as alleged by the writ petitioner, it is irrelevant so long as they are Malayalees and they do not act prejudicial to the interest of the Malayalam speaking linguistic minority residing in Tamil Nadu ,” the Court said. items.title: RPNLUP denies irregularities in recruitment, files police complaint over defamatory press coverage
items.summary: Dr Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLUP) has issued a press note calling coverage of its recent Assistant Professor appointments defamatory. The press note was issued on August 20 and was signed by the University's registrar. It says that RPNLUP has filed a complaint against those responsible for the defamatory media reports. "Dr. Rajendra Prasad National Law University (RPNLUP), Prayagraj, takes serious note and unequivocally condemns, the circulation and publication of misleading, criminally intimidating, derogatory and defamatory statements, imputations and insinuations on social media and news platforms concerning the recent appointment of Assistant Professors at the University," the note reads. The note has been issued amid a reported State Law Department inquiry and at least two complaints. RPNLUP had advertised 12 Assistant Professor (Law) posts in March this year. Interviews for the posts were held between July 22 and 30. According to a report , the State of Uttar Pradesh's Additional Law Remembrancer, also a member of the University's Executive Council (EC), had sought records and explanations from the University's Registrar on the recruitment process. In that letter, he allegedly mentioned that complete information regarding the appointments was not placed before the EC during its meeting on July 31, because of which he and another EC member abstained from voting on the appointments. The report said that the Additional Law Remembrancer asked whether shortlisting and selection committee formation adhered to University Grants Commission (UGC) regulations, and whether an academic-score chart in the prescribed format was prepared. Separately, a complaint reportedly to the Chief Minister alleged that that three of the Vice Chancellor's (VC) former students were among those selected during the process. Another complaint, addressed to the UGC Chairman and copied to Bar & Bench , also sought a stay on one candidate's appointment and an independent inquiry, alleging the candidate's joining was permitted without the Registrar's signature. It questioned the VC's role in the process and raised fear that records may have been altered after objections were first raised. It also alleged pressure on University officials and has asked the UGC to verify the selection against academic criteria and to independently check the candidate's EWS certificate.

items.title: Jharkhand High Court stays State order to cancel JPSC exams
items.summary: The Jharkhand High Court on Thursday stayed the State government's recent orders to cancel various recruitments undertaken by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JKPSC) [Deepmala & Ors v State of Jharkhand & Ors[ The State government had taken the decision following student protests over alleged irregularities in the examinations held by the recruiting agencies. However, the decision was challenged by various petitioners, including the successful candidates. These included candidates who had succeeded in the State Civil Services and Food Safety Officer examinations. Justice Deepak Roshan today granted interim relief to the candidates after hearing at least three petitions. He directed that all successful be allowed to continue their work till disposal of the case. "So far as the issue of interim protection is concerned; this Court feels that interest of justice and balance of convenience is paramount and in the instant case, the balance of convenience is in favour of the petitioners; inasmuch as, in effect they have been terminated without following any due process of law. Further, operation of this notification is also against public interest," the Court said. It added that regular appointments cannot be disturbed or terminated without following principles of natural justice and that the government order did not reflect any material to justify such drastic steps. The Court also observed that there was no material to show which candidates were involved in corruption. The matter will be heard next on September 15. The government had cancelled 22 examinations conducted by JPSC, JSSC and outsourced agencies. Jharkhand had witnessed a 26-day agitation against irregularities in government exams. The agitation was called off only after the government agreed to various demands of the students. items.title: Kerala: Clip from play on Emergency-era torture circulated as obscene, actor reacts
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A Malayalam play titled Misa, staged as part of the Democratic Youth Federation of India’s (DYFI) 16th state conference in Thrissur, has triggered a controversy after certain scenes were recorded and misrepresented on social media. DYFI is the youth wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], and Misa was conceptualised and performed by Chilanka Floating Theatre, a Kozhikode-based theatre group. The play tells the story of Snehalata Reddy, an artist who faced state torture during the Emergency in 1975, touching upon political oppression, exploitation of workers, and the suppression of dissent during that period. The title Misa is a take on the now repealed Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), which gave the government enormous powers to detain individuals. The controversy began after social media profiles linked to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Congress, and Sangh Parivar circulated the clip of a particular scene from the play, depicting the custodial torture Snehalata endured. In it, the actor is seen wearing a saree blouse and shorts, symbolically enacting how Snehalata was forced to walk naked and tortured by the police. At the end of the clip, the actor is also seen wearing a jail uniform. The scene was recorded, edited with music and shared on social media, claiming it to be a derogatory dance performance, triggering a slew of obscene comments and cyber trolling in the comment boxes. Among those who shared these clips are the BJP’s district-level chiefs. ML Ashwini, BJP Kasaragod district president, posted the video with a caption: “Is this how SFI, DYFI and their parent organisation seek to attract and engage the youth? A revealing reflection of the kind of culture and politics being promoted in the name of a youth organisation.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ashwini M L (@m.l._ashwini) Attempt to silence the political message Chinnus Chilanka, the actor who portrayed Snehalata Reddy, told TNM that what has transpired is not merely a matter of morality or obscenity, but an attempt to silence the political message being expressed. “Their problem is the politics in it. items.title: Muthanga struggle: Kerala HC suspends sentence of Geethanandan, 3 others
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday, August 21, suspended the sentence of four, including social activist M Geethanandan, in the Muthanga land struggle case of 2003. Justice A Badharudeen also granted bail to the four convicts who were awarded five years rigorous imprisonment by a trial court on July 31 in connection with an attempted murder of two government officers during the agitation. The order came on the appeal filed by Adivasi Gothra Mahasabha founder Geethanandan and other three convicts Binu, Sundaran, and Rameshan. The sessions court, Kalpetta had found the four guilty of abduction and attempts to murder police officer Abdul Salam and forest officer Sasidharan during the Muthanga agitation. The trial court verdict had triggered discussions over tribal communities’ unresolved struggles for land. While hearing the appeal on August 6, Justice Badharudeen had remarked that the judgement would require “thorough scrutiny”. The Muthanga tribal agitation was launched by Adivasi families under the banner of the Adivasi Gothra Mahasabha after the government delayed the distribution of five acres of land for landless tribal families, which it had promised in 2001. The agitation was led by Geethanandan and tribal leader CK Janu. It turned violent on February 19, 2003 when police and the Forest Department launched a joint operation to evict the protesters who had occupied parts of the Muthanga reserve forest in an attempt to claim the land promised to them. In the ensuing clash, policeman KV Vinod and tribal protester Jogi died while multiple persons suffered injuries. The trial court had let off the accused, including Geethanandan, in the Vinod murder case. It found only one tribal activist - Ashokan - guilty of Vinod’s murder. However, Ashokan had passed away during the trial.

items.title: A Karnataka-TN flashpoint? Why the shooting of 3 alleged poachers has escalated
items.summary: The shooting of three alleged poachers by Karnataka Forest Department personnel in Chamarajanagar on August 15 has since escalated into a larger conflict involving allegations of a fake encounter, attacks on forest infrastructure and protests in both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The three men, Anthony Swamy, John Rose Peter and Kumar Sawariyappan, were shot dead in the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in the early hours of August 15. A fourth man, Joseph Mahima Das, who was allegedly with them, survived and later released a video disputing the Forest Department’s account of the incident. The Forest Department maintains that the men were suspected poachers who opened fire at personnel during an anti-poaching operation and that the officers responded in self-defence. The families of the deceased, however, say the men had gone into the forest looking for missing cattle and were not poaching. The controversy has also taken on an interstate dimension because the three men were Tamil-speaking residents of villages in Karnataka. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has condemned the killings and sought a probe, while Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has rejected demands for a CBI investigation and said Tamil Nadu should not interfere in Karnataka’s affairs. Days after the shooting, several anti-poaching camps in the Cauvery and adjoining Male Mahadeshwara wildlife sanctuaries were allegedly vandalised or blown up with explosives. A forest fire also damaged around 10 acres in the Shilubepura area. So, what exactly happened and why has this become a Karnataka-Tamil Nadu flashpoint? What happened on August 15? According to the Forest Department, they received information around 8 pm on August 14 that a group of men had entered the sanctuary to hunt. Two teams of forest staff, comprising 10 to 15 personnel in total, were formed and sent into the Hanur forest range to track them down. Patrol staff at the Ganigamangala watch tower reportedly spotted people moving through the forest with torchlights, and the group was tracked through the night to a rocky outcrop known as Karadikalu, an area with mobile network coverage where the men are believed to have rested. When forest personnel approached the spot around 5 am, officials say one of the men opened fire on them, prompting a forest guard to fire back with a slide-action shotgun. items.title: Vizag: Six-yr-old school kid collapses and dies soon after being slapped by teacher
items.summary: A six-year-old boy, Pranay Tej, died after collapsing in a classroom, soon after a teacher scolded and slapped him. The incident, captured on CCTV, happened on August 20 at the Little Garden School in Visakhapatnam, where Pranay was a UKG student. The visuals show the boy sitting on a bench across from the teacher, seeming distressed and asking not to be called to the front. When he went to the teacher apparently without having done some assigned work on his slate, she was seen shaking the boy and trying to unbutton his shirt. She then slapped him, and within seconds, he collapsed onto her. The child was taken to the King George Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The exact cause of his death is yet to be confirmed through a post-mortem examination. Pranay’s mother Sai Lakshmi told the media that her son said he was scared before leaving for school in the morning, saying his teacher might hit him for not doing his homework. “The teacher tried to strip him and hit him for not doing some work. He's just a UKG kid, what is the need to intimidate and hit him like that,” the mother said. While Pranay collapsed around 11 am, the parents said they were informed by the school management nearly two hours later. The family staged a protest at the school demanding action against the school management and others responsible for the boy’s death. Nara Lokesh, Minister for Human Resources Development (Education) in Andhra Pradesh, said the government would take action against the school management. “It is heartbreaking that six-year-old Pranay Tej lost his life due to a teacher beating him at Little Garden Private School in Visakhapatnam. We are taking legal action against the culprits and the school management. I convey my deepest condolences to Pranay Tej’s parents. Stay strong. The loss you have suffered is irreplaceable by anyone. items.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy denied permission by MEA to visit USA
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy has been forced to cancel the US leg of his overseas tour after the Ministry of External Affairs denied political clearance for his visit, stating that “clearance from political angle is denied”. CM Revanth, who is currently in London, will now return to Hyderabad on August 23 instead of travelling to Boston and New York. His original itinerary included a visit to New York, where he was scheduled to attend an Indian Overseas Congress meet-and-greet. He was expected to return to Hyderabad on August 30. The Telangana government had sought the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) led Union government’s approval for the Chief Minister’s visits to both the UK and the US in accordance with established protocol. While permission was granted for the UK leg, clearance for the US visit was withheld. The decision was conveyed to the state government after the official delegation had already reached the UK. Reacting sharply to the Union government’s decision, CM Revanth said the proposed US visit was aimed at attracting leading global educational institutions to Telangana and strengthening the state’s position as a knowledge and skills hub. “The only purpose of the visit was to, as part of the New Education Policy of the Centre, bring the world’s best institutions to India, to Telangana, to Hyderabad,” he said, adding that such partnerships could have helped meet the aspirations of young people seeking world-class education, skills and training. Expressing shock over what he termed a ‘political denial’, CM Revanth said the proposed engagements were intended to advance Telangana’s development agenda and contribute to the broader goal of a “Viksit Bharat”. Despite cancelling his own US visit, the CM has directed state officials to proceed with the planned engagements in the US and complete the proposed memoranda of understanding (MoUs) and partnership agreements. items.title: Karnataka SIR: 43.8 lakh notices to be issued, Bengaluru accounts for 24 lakh
items.summary: The Karnataka Election Commission will issue notices to 43.8 lakh voters during the next phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Bengaluru accounts for more than half of recipients, with 24.05 lakh voters across its four electoral districts set to receive notices. Of these, 20.35 lakh voters have been flagged for “logical discrepancies” in their enumeration forms, while 23.45 lakh could not provide mapping details from the 2002 electoral roll. The notices will be issued after draft electoral rolls are published on August 24. The claims and objections period will continue until September 23, while their disposal will continue until October 22. The Chief Electoral Officer’s office has identified nine categories of logical discrepancies. These include implausible age gaps between parents and children, discrepancies in fathers’ names and differences between current and previous electoral records. Other categories include age gaps between siblings, unusually high numbers of children mapped to a parent, and discrepancies in voters’ own names between the current roll and the previous SIR. A voter may also be flagged if a parent linked to their record is later marked invalid in the current electoral roll. In such cases, all progeny records mapped to that parent’s previous SIR record will also be treated as anomalous. The “no mapping” category covers voters who could not provide details from the 2002 SIR or could not establish their linkage to voters included in that exercise. Notices will be served through Booth Level Officers from August 31. Each notice will specify the date, time and location where the voter must appear for verification. Voters will be required to submit documents establishing their identity, citizenship and residency. Two documents apart from Aadhaar will be sought, depending on the nature of the discrepancy. The notices will also contain a scanner allowing voters to upload the required forms online. However, voters will have to appear in person with physical copies of their documents for verification. Officials said voters would receive two notices. Those who fail to respond could be removed from the electoral roll and would then have to submit Form 6 for inclusion. The verification process will also involve photographs being taken when notices are served, when voters appear before the Electoral Registration Officer and when documents are submitted. items.title: Ex-SC Judge from Telangana to head panel probing NEET protest police excesses
items.summary: The Supreme Court has formed a five-member High-Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) headed by former judge R Subhash Reddy to probe alleged police excesses during NEET protests. The order was issued on July 18 but made public only on Thursday, August 20. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the panel to examine allegations of police excesses, violence against protesters and counter-allegations of violence and vandalism by demonstrators during the protests. The committee will examine 12 issues, including the use of pellet guns, electric batons, lathicharge and tear gas, alleged violence and harassment of women protesters, surveillance of demonstrators, the use of prohibitory orders and the invocation of Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. R Subhash Reddy, who will head the committee, served as a judge of the Andhra Pradesh High Court before his elevation to the Supreme Court in 2018. He was the first judge from Telangana to be elevated to the Supreme Court and retired in January 2022. The other members of the committee are former Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi High Court judge Justice Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP LR Bishnoi. The Supreme Court directed the committee to submit its first interim report at the earliest on allegations of excessive force against protesters and alleged targeted violence, harassment, molestation and secondary victimisation of women protesters. The court said the panel will also examine the police chain of command to identify those responsible for directions that allegedly led to excessive use of force. The committee will consider whether interim compensation should be awarded to injured protesters and police personnel. According to a police affidavit, 248 police personnel and 218 protesters were injured during the July 20 demonstrations. Police attributed the violence to criminal elements who allegedly infiltrated the student protesters. The panel will also examine whether pellet guns and other metallic kinetic projectiles should be banned during crowd-control operations, given the serious injuries they can cause. Other issues include whether police and security personnel should be required to wear uniforms and visible nameplates during crowd-control operations to ensure individual accountability, and whether surveillance of protesters was consistent with their rights

items.title: Jana Sena MP’s son served only a notice after crashing car, killing woman in Hyderabad
items.summary: Lingamaneni Sanjush (21), the son of Andhra Pradesh Rajya Sabha MP Lingamaneni Ramesh, was served notice by the Cyberabad police after being named as the accused in a road accident that killed a 26-year-old woman in Hyderabad’s Madhapur on August 16. Sanjush was allegedly driving an Aston Martin at a high speed when the car hit Bharati Mukhi, a sales associate at a Lifestyle store in the Inorbit Mall in Madhapur, Hyderabad. Bharati was crossing the road while bringing lunch from a place nearby and returning to work, according to the complaint filed by the store manager Aswin Kumar. Madhapur ACP Ch Sridhar said Sanjush was not arrested because the offence registered against him is bailable and carries a maximum punishment of less than seven years. Police only served him a notice, he said. Sanjush was booked under Section 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita – causing death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide – which carries a maximum punishment of five years’ imprisonment and a fine. “As the punishment is below seven years, it is bailable. We have served notices to the accused. He has not been arrested,” Sridhar said. According to the FIR, Bharati and her colleague Pooja Ashok, both aged 26, had gone to the vicinity of ITC Kohenur at around 3 pm to collect lunch. While returning to Inorbit Mall, Bharati was crossing the road in front of the mall when the Aston Martin, bearing registration number TG-09-G-0666, allegedly hit her. Bharati suffered severe bleeding injuries to her head and was taken to Apollo Hospital in Jubilee Hills in the same car. Doctors examined her and declared her dead. Pooja later informed Lifestyle store manager Panjala Ashwin Kumar about the accident. Ashwin reached the hospital and subsequently approached the police, based on whose complaint the case was registered. Police later identified Sanjush as the person allegedly driving the vehicle at the time of the accident. The Aston Martin has been seized, while police reportedly conducted drunk-driving tests on Sanjush. His blood samples were also collected and sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for analysis. Police are awaiting the post-mortem examination report and said they are collecting further evidence as part of the investigation. Records show that the Aston Martin is registered in the name of Honor Prime Housing LLP. The circumstances in which Sanjush was driving the vehicle at the time of the crash are also being examined.
